accepted_units.title: Path measures, time marginals, endpoint laws, and bridges retain different information
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes a full path law from its one-time flow and endpoint joint law, then reconstructs it as a mixture of conditional bridges. This makes explicit which correlations a projection forgets and which conditional object must be retained for reconstruction.
accepted_units.context_note: This is foundational notation rather than a new theorem, but it is a reusable semantic account of projection, information loss, and disintegration.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The decomposition requires Polish path and state spaces so regular conditional bridge measures exist; time marginals alone cannot recover cross-time correlations.

accepted_units.title: The entropy chain rule reduces path optimization to endpoints and preserves reference bridges
accepted_units.why_material: Disintegrating relative entropy into endpoint entropy plus expected conditional bridge entropy proves equality of the static and dynamic infima and shows that the optimizer changes only the endpoint coupling while keeping every reference bridge unchanged.
accepted_units.context_note: Strict convexity supplies at-most-one solutions. The proof is explicit and should be kept distinct from the introductory summary of the same result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The reduction depends on conditioning by the endpoint map, the additive entropy formula on Polish spaces, finite entropy for the equality case, and fixed endpoint marginals.

accepted_units.title: Reference tilting and compactness give an existence criterion for unbounded entropy projections
accepted_units.why_material: An unbounded reference is exponentially tilted to a probability reference; on the fixed-marginal constraint set the correction is constant, so lower semicontinuity and compactness reduce existence to the presence of one finite-entropy feasible point.
accepted_units.context_note: The source also gives practical sufficient marginal and integrability conditions. Several weights and integrals are typographically damaged, so exact hypotheses need PDF verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The argument uses tightness of fixed-marginal couplings on Polish spaces, a coercive integrable weight, lower semicontinuity of entropy, and invariance of the objective up to a constraint-dependent constant.

accepted_units.title: Additive endpoint potentials dualize fixed-marginal entropy minimization
accepted_units.why_material: The fixed marginal constraints are recognized exactly by test functions that split over the two coordinates, yielding a convex dual problem whose attained equality exposes an exponential density for the optimizer.
accepted_units.context_note: Dual equality is cited in the stated function spaces, while dual attainment is explicitly not guaranteed in general; the product-density conclusion is conditional on attainment and positivity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The dual variables live in weighted continuous-function spaces, and the tensor-sum form follows specifically from two coordinate marginal constraints and the variational representation of entropy.

accepted_units.title: Support geometry and measurability obstruct naive product factorization
accepted_units.why_material: The source identifies two independent failures of a formal exponential product representation: the optimizer may live on a nonrectangular support, and a jointly measurable tensor sum need not have separately measurable factors. Intrinsic-core perturbation and absolute-continuity hypotheses repair the respective failures.
accepted_units.context_note: The resulting theorem gives sufficient, not necessary, conditions for a measurable product density and a coupled marginal system. It explicitly warns that outside the internal regime the density can be structurally more complex.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Factorization depends on support relative to the reference, intrinsic-core placement of the constraint, and comparison between the endpoint reference and a product of its marginals; it is not a consequence of formal algebra alone.

accepted_units.title: Entropy-minimizing recombination forces the Markov property
accepted_units.why_material: At any cut time, fixing the present distribution and the conditional past and future laws, the entropy-minimizing recombination makes past and future conditionally independent. Replacing a non-Markov candidate by this recombination preserves all time marginals while strictly lowering entropy.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof uses entropy disintegration and Jensen equality, providing a concrete local repair rather than relying on intuition that the optimum should inherit Markovity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The reference itself must be Markov, conditional measures must be well-defined through a sigma-finite time marginal, and the competitor class fixes both conditional halves and the cut-time marginal.

accepted_units.title: Markovity upgrades an endpoint density into a two-sided product transform
accepted_units.why_material: When both the reference and entropy optimizer are Markov and the endpoint density is sufficiently supported, a density depending jointly on the two endpoints factorizes into a nonnegative initial factor times a final factor, even without an internal constraint.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem records explicit regenerative and absolute-continuity hypotheses; it is a conditional structural result, not a universal factorization statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The upgrade uses a Markov reference, a bridge-density representation, a support/regeneration condition, common endpoint reference marginals, and the stated entropy-integrability assumptions.

accepted_units.title: A two-sided endpoint transform factorizes every intermediate marginal and preserves Markovity
accepted_units.why_material: Weighting a reversible Markov law by one initial and one final factor yields a time-symmetric transform whose intermediate density splits into a backward conditional expectation and a forward conditional expectation; conditional independence proves the transformed law remains Markov.
accepted_units.context_note: The source distinguishes sufficient finite-entropy conditions from the broader transform definition and notes that nonrectangular-support optimizers need not belong to this class.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The factorization of the intermediate density uses the Markov property of the reference and positive conditional integration; the forward and backward factors depend on opposite endpoint filtrations.

accepted_units.title: Carré-du-champ corrections translate endpoint weights into forward and backward dynamics
accepted_units.why_material: The forward and backward stochastic generators of a two-sided transform are obtained by adding carré-du-champ corrections determined by opposite conditional factors; logarithms of those factors convert linear heat equations into nonlinear Hamilton-Jacobi-type equations.
accepted_units.context_note: The source labels the general generator formula informal and points to a separate rigorous treatment; the derivation is an idea-of-proof, while standard diffusion and graph cases are said to follow rigorously under regularity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The formulas require a Markov generator, functions in its and the carré-du-champ domains, positive intermediate densities, and sufficient regularity; exact arrows and multiline equations are damaged in extraction.

accepted_units.title: Finite entropy becomes kinetic drift action for diffusions
accepted_units.why_material: Girsanov's entropy identity and a superposition result convert path-space entropy minimization into a constrained minimal-action problem for marginal flows and drift fields; uniqueness of the path optimizer and an orthogonal-projection argument determine the optimal drift.
accepted_units.context_note: The proposition is stated for Brownian reference under finite moment and entropy assumptions. Displayed PDE and integral notation needs exact-source verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This equivalence depends on diffusion noise, quadratic drift cost, the weak Fokker-Planck constraint, Girsanov theory, and a superposition theorem; it is not a representation-free identity.

accepted_units.title: Convex jump action is the graph analogue of diffusion kinetic action
accepted_units.why_material: Replacing the Laplacian by a reversible graph jump generator turns gradient drifts into multiplicative edge-rate tilts and quadratic action into the convex conjugate of exponential increments, while preserving the same marginal-flow optimization pattern.
accepted_units.context_note: The graph proposition follows the diffusion proof scheme and makes the representation change explicit; the statement contains a likely source typo in the displayed state-space label and formula extraction damage.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The analogue uses a countable locally finite connected graph, bounded total jump rates, a reversible measure, edge currents, and the convex pair associated with exponential rate changes.

accepted_units.title: Slowing a reference process converts entropic duality into transport duality
accepted_units.why_material: A large-deviation principle for a slowed Markov reference and the Laplace-Varadhan lemma transform log-integral dual objectives into a supremal path constraint; contraction over endpoint-fixed paths yields the transport cost and Kantorovich dual constraint.
accepted_units.context_note: The source repeatedly labels this presentation heuristic or informal and refers elsewhere for rigorous Gamma-convergence. The mechanism is retained as an asymptotic derivation, not asserted here as a proved theorem under unspecified hypotheses.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The limit requires a specified speed and path-space rate function, suitable Laplace-Varadhan hypotheses, contraction to an endpoint cost, and compactness/equicoercivity beyond pointwise dual convergence.

accepted_units.title: Gamma convergence transfers minima and entropic regularization selects a unique transport limit
accepted_units.why_material: Equicoercive Gamma convergence carries optimal values and minimizers to the limiting transport problem; in the graph case, the entropic sequence further selects a unique path law among infinitely many geodesic-path minimizers through a secondary entropy minimization.
accepted_units.context_note: The general Gamma-convergence facts are standard context, while the graph theorem is cited as a rigorous result. Selection is solver/reference conditional, not intrinsic uniqueness of the unregularized transport problem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The transfer uses narrow topology, equicoercivity, a slowed graph walk with its large-deviation rate, and a residual reference measure supported on geodesic paths.

accepted_units.title: Rare-event conditioning selects the entropy projection
accepted_units.why_material: Large deviations of empirical path measures turn conditioning on an atypical final marginal into minimization of relative entropy under endpoint constraints; shrinking the conditioning neighborhood then concentrates on the unique entropy projection.
accepted_units.context_note: The derivation is explicitly informal and cites rigorous large-deviation results. The finite three-point calculation is only an illustration of the rate function and is not treated as model-visible arithmetic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The interpretation depends on independent particles, an empirical-measure large-deviation principle, compact entropy sublevels, strict convexity, and the order of the large-population and shrinking-neighborhood limits.

accepted_units.title: Second entropy variation links entropic interpolation to curvature operators
accepted_units.why_material: The source contrasts heuristic entropy convexity along transport geodesics with a rigorous second-derivative formula along entropic interpolations, expressing curvature information through forward and backward potentials and an iterated generator operator.
accepted_units.context_note: The Riemannian transport formula is described as arising from Otto's heuristic calculus; the entropic formulas are attributed to a cited work and one graph-curvature implication remains an expectation, not an established conclusion here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The identities depend on differentiability of entropy along the chosen interpolation, reversible generator calculus, regular two-sided potentials, and the diffusion-specific reduction from the generalized operator to the usual iterated carré du champ.

accepted_units.title: Reciprocity weakens Markov conditional independence while preserving time symmetry
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes conditioning the path interior on its two boundary states from conditioning future and past on a single present state, showing a strict hierarchy: every Markov law is reciprocal, but not conversely.
accepted_units.context_note: This mathematical distinction appears inside a historical survey and is retained because it clarifies the structural role of the stronger Markov conclusion for entropy optimizers.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Both notions are formulated on path segments and conditional laws; reciprocity depends on two boundary states, whereas Markovity depends on one separating present state.

accepted_units.title: Noise turns deterministic transport control into entropy-minimizing stochastic control
accepted_units.why_material: For Brownian reference, the entropy problem is represented as minimizing expected quadratic control action subject to endpoint laws, and the zero-noise limit connects this stochastic control formulation to deterministic dynamic transport.
accepted_units.context_note: The survey cites the control and zero-noise results and explicitly warns that the convergence is unclear for nonquadratic Lagrangians; this limitation is part of the unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The clean bridge relies on Brownian noise, quadratic action matched to Girsanov entropy, admissible progressively measurable controls, and a zero-noise limit.

accepted_units.title: Exponential reference change defines entropy for sigma-finite measures without changing its intrinsic value
accepted_units.why_material: A sigma-finite reference is normalized by an exponential weight, and entropy is corrected by the expected weight and normalizer; the source proves the value is independent of the admissible weight and retains strict convexity and variational lower semicontinuity.
accepted_units.context_note: This appendix supplies the exact foundation used earlier for unbounded path measures. Formula layout is damaged but the reference-change invariant and variational characterization are readable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The definition requires a sigma-finite reference, an exponential weight with finite normalizer, finite weight expectation under the candidate probability, and a topology/function class compatible with the variational formula.
